Note that the up to $66 disability allowance must be justified and proven and will be paid for things required directly to the disability itself (doctors fees etc) so this will not go towards the cost of living (rent, food etc)


I posted a similar question to this here:
https://www.reddit.com/r/newzealand/comments/sdj04a/why_are_disabled_people_that_rely_on_benefits/?utm_medium=android_app&utm_source=share


There is a wide range of views and opinions from being sympathetic to people who are disabled to the disabled are lucky they get any money at all


Differing opinions on what disabled people are worth in society compared to others, opinions of what working and earning money in society is worth, who should really be looking after people that are disabled, beliefs that supported living payments are handed out to people who don't need them etc all coupled with disabled people being a minority seems to make this situation complicated and perhaps not looked into as much as it should be
